title: Reverse a Linked List
statement:
Reverse a singly linked list by relinking it, and return the
new head.

## Your function

```
struct node {
    int value;
    struct node *next;
};

struct node *reverse_list(struct node *head);
```

The struct is declared in your file and in the harness -- copy it exactly as
above. Afterwards the last node is the head and every `next` points the other
way.

## Watch out

- Relink the nodes. Copying the values into an array, reversing that and
  writing them back gives the right output and dodges the entire exercise.
- Three pointers: the node before, the node you are on, and the node after.
  Save `head->next` **before** you overwrite it, or the rest of the list is
  gone and no amount of care afterwards gets it back.
- The empty list is `NULL`, and reversing it gives `NULL`. A one-node list
  comes back unchanged.
- The old head becomes the new tail, so its `next` has to end up `NULL`.
- Do not allocate anything, and do not free anything -- the caller owns the
  nodes and will free the list you hand back.

tests.name: empty list
tests.description: head is NULL. Return NULL without following it.

tests.name: one node
tests.description: The head is already the tail. Its next must end up NULL, which it already is.

tests.name: two nodes
tests.description: The smallest list where the links actually change.
